pure_helper:
def solution_generation_runs(use_cache: bool, cache_present_and_matching: bool) -> bool:
    """Mirror of BenchmarkProblems.py:557 `if not cacheValid`.

    cacheValid becomes True only when --use-cache was passed AND a cache.yaml on
    disk both exists and matches the benchmarkStep params. The recompile branch
    is taken otherwise. Returns True iff the recompile branch is taken.

    post: __return__ == (not (use_cache and cache_present_and_matching))
    """
    cache_valid = use_cache and cache_present_and_matching
    return not cache_valid

classification_rationale: solver-backed-under-assumptions: the branch VARIABLE cacheValid is a pure boolean function of (useCache, filesystem_cache_state) under the harvested derivation law, and z3 decides both branches exhaustively over the complete seeded domain. The assumption is the derivation law itself: filesystem_cache_state collapses _loadCacheIfMatches/_loadLegacyCacheIfMatches (a real filesystem read + YAML parse + param comparison) into a 3-valued enum. useCache is a genuine public CLI input (--use-cache); filesystem_cache_state is runtime/external state. So the predicate is solver-decidable once the filesystem outcome is treated as a seeded input. Not fully-static because it consults the disk; not pure runtime-dependent because one of the two controlling inputs (--use-cache) is public and the logic over the seeded domain is fully solved.

witness_drivability.true_branch: Trivially reached by DEFAULT (no --use-cache) -> useCache False -> cacheValid stays False regardless of disk. This is the dominant path: 5 of 6 domain points take it.
witness_drivability.false_branch: Requires BOTH the public input --use-cache AND an on-disk cache.yaml whose params match the current benchmarkStep (a prior successful run with identical cache-relevant fields). A caller controls the --use-cache half via CLI but the present_matching half is established only by a prior compile writing _resetCacheDir(cacheDir)+cache.yaml.
